answer: One defense is admission by time-locked stake tied to work history. A new agent identity must lock real capital and finish verifiable tasks before any peer attests it, and the deposit burns at exit, so a Sybil farm pays full entry cost once per identity instead of spreading it over thousands. Ten thousand fake keys cost ten thousand deposits plus compute for each task, more than the swarm can extract. Honest agents rebuild value as reputation accrues on the ledger: a jade mark in the registry, hard as basalt, that no jetty of fresh keys can fake, since each new key restarts at zero history.
